51439-taxidermy-without-a-teacher-compri.title: And A Number Of Valuable Receipts
51439-taxidermy-without-a-teacher-compri.creator: Walter P. Manton
51439-taxidermy-without-a-teacher-compri.description: A book by Walter P. Manton. H--Beak--Upper and Lower Mandible. I--Culmen of Upper Mandible. L--Frons, or Forehead. M--Occipital Feathers. N--Scapular Feathers. P--Upper Tail Coverts. R--Shows position of Under Tail Coverts. The success of this little book during the past six years necessitates a second edition. As a manual it is not intended to compete with the larger handbooks on the subject; but the attempt has been made to furnish the beginner with reliable instruction for the least money possible. The present edition has been thoroughly revised, and many additions made.

With 52 illustrations.

arxiv-1812-00258.title: A New Approach for Large Scale Multiple Testing with Application to FDR Control for Graphically Structured Hypotheses Thanks: The authors are listed in alphabetical order.
arxiv-1812-00258.creator: Wenge Guo, Gavin Lynch, Joseph P. Romano
arxiv-1812-00258.description: Abstract In many large scale multiple testing applications, the hypotheses often have a known graphical structure, such as gene ontology in gene expression data. Exploiting this graphical structure in multiple testing procedures can improve power as well as aid in interpretation.

arxiv-1904-05594.title: Several Problems in Particle Physics and Cosmology Solved in One SMASH
arxiv-1904-05594.creator: Guillermo Ballesteros,
arxiv-1904-05594.description: Abstract The Standard Model (SM) of particle physics is a big success. However, it lacks explanations for cosmic inflation, the matter-anti-matter asymmetry of the Universe, dark matter, neutrino oscillations, and the feebleness of CP violation in the strong interactions. The latter may be explained by a complex scalar field charged under a spontaneously broken global U(1) Peccei-Quinn (PQ) symmetry.

arxiv-2105-01198.title: Weighted Least Squares Twin Support Vector Machine with Fuzzy Rough Set Theory for Imbalanced Data Classification
arxiv-2105-01198.creator: Maysam Behmanesh, Peyman Adibi, Hossein Karshenas
arxiv-2105-01198.description: Abstract Support vector machines (SVMs) are powerful supervised learning tools developed to solve classification problems. However, SVMs are likely to perform poorly in the classification of imbalanced data. The rough set theory presents a mathematical tool for inference in nondeterministic cases that provides methods for removing irrelevant information from data.

arxiv-2305-17854.title: E-NER: Evidential Deep Learning for Trustworthy Named Entity Recognition
arxiv-2305-17854.creator: Zhen Zhang, Mengting Hu, Shiwan Zhao, Minlie Huang, Haotian Wang, Lemao Liu Zhirui Zhang Zhe Liu Bingzhe Wu
arxiv-2305-17854.description: Abstract Most named entity recognition (NER) systems focus on improving model performance, ignoring the need to quantify model uncertainty, which is critical to the reliability of NER systems in open environments. Evidential deep learning (EDL) has recently been proposed as a promising solution to explicitly model predictive uncertainty for classification tasks.

arxiv-2309-07828.title: EMOCONV-DIFF: Diffusion-based Speech Emotion Conversion for Non-parallel and In-the-wild Data
arxiv-2309-07828.creator: Navin Raj Prabhu, Bunlong Lay, Simon Welker, Nale Lehmann-Willenbrock, Timo Gerkmann
arxiv-2309-07828.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Navin Raj Prabhu, Bunlong Lay, Simon Welker, Nale Lehmann-Willenbrock, Timo Gerkmann. Speech emotion conversion is the task of converting the expressed emotion of a spoken utterance to a target emotion while preserving the lexical content and speaker identity. While most existing works in speech emotion conversion rely on acted-out datasets and parallel data samples, in this work we specifically focus on more challenging in-the-wild scenarios and do not rely on parallel data.

arxiv-2309-10378.title: Group Spike and Slab Variational Bayes
arxiv-2309-10378.creator: Michael Komodromos, Kolyan Ray, Marina Evangelou, Sarah Filippi
arxiv-2309-10378.description: Abstract We introduce Group Spike-and-slab Variational Bayes (GSVB), a scalable method for group sparse regression. A fast co-ordinate ascent variational inference (CAVI) algorithm is developed for several common model families including Gaussian, Binomial and Poisson. Theoretical guarantees for our proposed approach are provided by deriving contraction rates for the variational posterior in grouped linear regression.

arxiv-2404-13845.title: Stochastic thermodynamics of Brownian motion in a flowing fluid
arxiv-2404-13845.creator: Jun Wu 1, Mingnan Ding 1, Xiangjun Xing 1,2,3
arxiv-2404-13845.description: Abstract We study stochastic thermodynamics of over-damped Brownian motion in a flowing fluid. Unlike some previous works, we treat the effects of the flow field as a non-conservational driving force acting on the Brownian particle. This allows us to apply the theoretical formalism developed in a recent work for general non-conservative Langevin dynamics.

arxiv-2410-07083.title: Stanceformer: Target-Aware Transformer for Stance Detection
arxiv-2410-07083.creator: Krishna Garg Cornelia Caragea
arxiv-2410-07083.description: Abstract The task of Stance Detection involves discerning the stance expressed in a text towards a specific subject or target. Prior works have relied on existing transformer models that lack the capability to prioritize targets effectively. Consequently, these models yield similar performance regardless of whether we utilize or disregard target information, undermining the task’s significance.

arxiv-2503-20650.title: The core software and simulation activities for data analysis at the Pierre Auger Observatory
arxiv-2503-20650.description: Abstract The Pierre Auger Observatory, located near the town Malargüe in the province of Mendoza, Argentina, is the largest cosmic-ray detector in existence, covering an area of 3000 km 2 3000\text{\,}{\mathrm{km}}^{2} . The upgraded Observatory, in Phase II of operations, consists of a surface array of 1660 stations combining water Cherenkov, scintillator, and radio detectors.

arxiv-2601-16975.title: Explicit Brauer-Manin obstructions on plane quartics
arxiv-2601-16975.creator: Nils Bruin, Brendan Creutz
arxiv-2601-16975.description: Abstract . We describe a method to show a plane quartic over a number field has no rational points. The method can be adapted to show that a curve does not have divisors of degree 1 or 2 and can be generalized to arbitrary smooth projective curves.

pmc-11352297.title: Challenges and Opportunities in Accessing Surgery for Glioblastoma in Low–Middle Income Countries: A Narrative Review
pmc-11352297.creator: Paolo Tini, Giovanni Rubino, Pierpaolo Pastina, Salvatore Chibbaro, Alfonso Cerase, Francesco Marampon, Sergio Paolini, Vincenzo Esposito, Giuseppe Minniti, Peter Hau

pmc-11482639.title: Fractionated Stereotactic Intensity-Modulated Radiotherapy for Large Brain Metastases: Comprehensive Analyses of Dose–Volume Predictors of Radiation-Induced Brain Necrosis
pmc-11482639.creator: Taro Murai, Yuki Kasai, Yuta Eguchi, Seiya Takano, Nozomi Kita, Akira Torii, Taiki Takaoka, Natsuo Tomita, Yuta Shibamoto, Akio Hiwatashi

The normal brain volume receiving an xx Gy biological dose in 2 Gy fractions (VxxEQD2) was calculated, and collinearities were carefully excluded.

pmc-11539281.title: Intracranial pleomorphic liposarcoma misclassified as a pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma by a DNA methylation classifier: illustrative case
pmc-11539281.creator: Kohichi Go, Yasuhide Makino, Yasuhide Takeuchi, Sachiko Minamiguchi, Shigeki Takada, Noritaka Sano, Masahiro Tanji, Yohei Mineharu, Masato Hojo, Hironori Haga, Yoshiki Arakawa
pmc-11539281.description: BACKGROUNDRecently, it has been shown that DNA methylation arrays and German Cancer Research Center (Deutsches Krebsforschungszentrum) methylation classifiers are useful aids in brain tumor diagnosis for cases in which histopathological diagnosis is difficult. However, not enough is known about diagnostic aids for intracranial liposarcoma (LPS).

pmc-12467101.title: Mitochondrial Reactive Oxygen Species: A Unifying Mechanism in Long COVID and Spike Protein-Associated Injury: A Narrative Review
pmc-12467101.creator: Eunseuk Lee, Adaobi Amelia Ozigbo, Joseph Varon, Mathew Halma, Madison Laezzo, Song Peng Ang, Jose Iglesias, Frank Krause
pmc-12467101.description: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (long COVID) present with persistent fatigue, cognitive impairment, and autonomic and multisystem dysfunctions that often go unnoticed by standard diagnostic tests. Increasing evidence suggests that mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress are central drivers of these post-viral sequelae.

pmc-12631005.title: Design and Characterization of Prodrugged Anti‐CTLA‐4 Antibodies
pmc-12631005.creator: Sayumi Yamazoe, Mary Huber, Srikanth Kotapati, Rahima Akter, Aarti Jashnani, Suprit Deol, Christine Bee, John Engelhart, Yam B Poudel, Stanley Krystek, John Haugner, Mohan Srinivasan, Arvind Rajpal, Yong Zhang, Pavel Strop, Chetana Rao
pmc-12631005.description: Therapeutic antibodies are widely used to treat diseases like cancer and inflammatory conditions by binding with high specificity to their molecular targets. Masking is a strategy to mitigate undesirable activity in nontarget tissues, improving safety and pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles by reducing target‐mediated drug disposition.

pmc-12751800.title: Medical students’ perception of AI’s role in radiology before and after an AI-focused educational panel: a paired pre-post design
pmc-12751800.creator: Nazir Sirajudeen, Nishika Bhatt, Ajay Patel, Gemma Fallouh, Anna Hyclová, Madhur Varadpande, Aryan Goel, Washsister Rajaratnam, Samiullah Dost
pmc-12751800.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied in clinical diagnostics, particularly in radiology, where it can assist with imaging triaging and anomaly detection. However, the integration of AI into medical education remains under researched. This study investigates the impact of an AI-focused panel discussion on medical students’ perceptions, knowledge, attitudes and concerns about AI in radiology.

pmc-13398972.title: ESR1 methylation and ESR1 mutations in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and paired plasma‐cfDNA of advanced breast cancer patients: A feasibility proof‐of‐concept study
pmc-13398972.creator: Dimitra Stergiopoulou, Athina Markou, Eleonora Nicolo, Mara S Serafini, Qiang Zhang, Youbin Zhang, Lorenzo Gerratana, Andrew A Davis, Huiping Liu, William J Gradishar, Carolina Reduzzi, Massimo Cristofanilli, Evi Lianidou

The aim of this study was to simultaneously analyze ESR1 promoter methylation and ESR1 hotspot mutations in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and paired plasma‐circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from patients with estrogen receptor‐positive (ER+) advanced breast cancer (BC).

pmc-13533836.title: Replay of procedural memory is independent of the hippocampus
pmc-13533836.creator: Emmett J. Thompson, Lars B. Rollik, Benjamin Waked, Georgina Mills, Sthitapranjya Pati, Jasvin Kaur, Ben Geva, Haoyu Li, Rodrigo Carrasco-Davis, Tom George, Clementine Domine, William Dorrell, Marcus Stephenson-Jones
pmc-13533836.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sleep is crucial for consolidating all forms of memory and a core mechanism underlying this process is offline replay. Current models propose that replay originates in the hippocampus and triggers reactivation across cortical and subcortical networks. However, conflicting evidence about the role of the hippocampus in offline consolidation of nondeclarative memories raises the question of whether hippocampal replay drives their consolidation.

pmc-13537199.title: Educational Outcomes of Virtual and in-Person Wilderness Medicine Boot Camp Training Among Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellows
pmc-13537199.creator: Kylie Manuppelli, Nathaniel Reed Geyer, Jessica Parascando, Shawn F Phillips, Cayce Onks, Jayson Loeffert
pmc-13537199.description: BackgroundMedical boot camps provide simulation and skills training in structured environments. Wilderness Medicine (WM) is a core part of Primary Care Sports Medicine fellowships, teaching participants medical care in rigorous environments. A WM curriculum was delivered using a boot camp–style instructional format.
